title: Phantom of the Masquerade: Graph Neural Network-Based Detection of Masquerade Attacks in Controller Area Networks
abstract: arXiv:2611.26094v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The lack of built-in security in controller area networks (CANs) exposes modern vehicles and industrial systems to masquerade attacks that can compromise safety and reliability. These attacks inject malicious messages that mimic legitimate communication patterns, making them difficult to detect using existing intrusion detection systems (IDS). Prior graph-based IDS approaches often rely on shallow embeddings that decouple representation learning from classification, which may limit their ability to fully exploit structural and signal-level information. In this paper, we propose PhantoMasq, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework for detecting masquerade attacks in CAN systems. PhantoMasq models CAN traffic as message sequence graphs enriched with lightweight statistical features derived from signal behavior, enabling joint learning of structural dependencies and temporal characteristics. The detection task is formulated as a graph

translated_title: 假面舞会上的幽灵：基于图神经网络的控制器局域网伪装攻击检测
translated_abstract: 控制器局域网（CAN）缺乏内置的安全机制，使得现代车辆和工业系统容易受到伪装攻击（masquerade attacks），这类攻击可能危及安全性与可靠性。这些攻击会注入模仿合法通信模式的恶意消息，导致现有入侵检测系统（IDS）难以检测。以往基于图的IDS方法通常依赖浅层嵌入，将表示学习与分类过程解耦，这可能限制了它们充分利用结构和信号级信息的能力。在本文中，我们提出了PhantoMasq，一个基于图神经网络（GNN）的CAN系统伪装攻击检测框架。PhantoMasq将CAN流量建模为消息序列图，并结合从信号行为中提取的轻量级统计特征，实现对结构依赖关系与时间特性的联合学习。检测任务被表述为图
tldr: 本文提出PhantoMasq框架，利用图神经网络将CAN流量建模为融合信号统计特征的消息序列图，联合学习结构依赖与时间特性，从而有效检测控制器局域网中难以识别的伪装攻击。
en_tdlr: We propose PhantoMasq, a GNN-based framework that models CAN traffic as message sequence graphs enriched with lightweight statistical signal features, jointly learning structural dependencies and temporal characteristics to effectively detect hard-to-spot masquerade attacks in Controller Area Networks.
